page.layout: One printed page, one text column (no margin notes). Running head at the top; numbered paragraphs I, II, III in the column; page number at top right; a catchword-like signature mark "x" at the foot of the column, with the word "uuntur," set at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: I. Quidâ dixerunt, causam materialem aquæ esse aerem, sicut etiam materia existit uentorū. Etenim quod ad causam formale attinet, uentum esse aerem motum ac fluitantem: aquam uerò esse similiter aerem, sed cōsistentem. Quam ob causam, cum omnis aer sit unus idemq; aer, ijdem censuerunt omnem uentum esse unum eundemque uentum, & omnem aquam siue omnia flumina esse unam eandemque aquam & unum idemq; flumen. Verum huius opinionis absurditas per se manifesta est.

II. Quidā imaginati sunt, in terra existere immensam aliquam uoraginē, ex qua tanquā publico penu fontes ac flumina aquarū dulcium hinc inde in omnes orbis partes deriuentur: sicut in humano corpore sanguis per uenas ab arce cordis in omnia membra emanat. Cū uerò ex his aquis semper ingens aquarū uis sursum educatur, rursumq; eadem in aquas recidat, eandē ubiq; aquā semper manere, nec ullam nouam procreari. Verum subsistere sententia hæc non potest. Si namque omnis aqua esset eadem aqua, sequeretur, aquam multò esse ampliorē uniuersa terra: quod absurdum est. Deinde, ubi immensa illa uorágo locum habet?

III. Aristoteli placet, eodē pacto aquam gigni in terra, quo gignitur in aere. Ascendunt autem in acrem uapores multi ac densi, qui ibi in uastas nubes coeunt: paulatim uerò accedēte frigore, in aquā resoluuntur.

page.notes: Printed text is in italic throughout; the paragraph numbers I., II., III. are roman. The text ends at "resoluuntur," which is followed by the catchword-like word "uuntur," as printed at the foot right. The "x" at the foot left is a signature mark. Doubtful readings: "existit" and "uentorū" are as printed; "uorágo" and "uoraginē" are as printed. The word "Quidā" in paragraph II has a tilde over the a as printed.
